stem: Greymont Foundry needs its build server and every engineer's laptop to install the identical provider build, byte for byte, every time `terraform init` runs, not merely a version that satisfies the same range. What guarantees that?

choices.text: A `~>` version constraint tight enough that only a single specific patch release could ever possibly match at any given time.
Have every engineer run `terraform init -upgrade` before each build, so each machine picks up the newest version that still matches the configured constraint.
The provider is downloaded once and manually copied into every machine's plugin cache folder.
A dependency lock file recording the exact version and checksum has been committed to version control and is present when `init` runs.

rationale: A committed dependency lock file records the exact version and checksum, so every `init` verifies against the same recorded build rather than merely a range. A tight `~>` constraint is still a range, and a new release could later appear that matches it, so it cannot guarantee the identical build over time. Running `terraform init -upgrade` explicitly tells Terraform to ignore the versions recorded in the dependency lock file and install the newest version that still matches the constraint, so two machines that run it on different days can still end up with different builds. Manually copying a downloaded provider into each machine's cache works once but is an error-prone manual process, not something `terraform init` itself verifies.
